- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast low by 5–10%.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast 3–5 days after spike at 1–2% below peak.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting trends; if sentiment shows moderate bullishness (0.33–0.67) and price is above 30-day moving average, slightly raise forecast to align with reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag in downward moves; if sentiment turns bearish mid-horizon, adjust forecast downward by 2–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33), model often overfits recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.
